claim: Free energies of isolated non-periodic crystallites of the same two-dimensional binary model, at like-to-unlike attraction ratio 0.1 and kT/E_AB = 0.06, cross at about 100 particles, square being favoured below and hexagonal above, although the lattice energy alone favours hexagonal at every size considered; the crossover comes from the finite-temperature terms, the surface entropy with a heat-capacity contribution to the surface internal energy.

numbers.name: crystallite_particle_count
numbers.note: the free-energy crossover size, stated as about 100.

validity_conditions: A MODEL RESULT, run in LAMMPS, not HOOMD. Two-dimensional 1:1 binary mixture with a short-ranged Fermi-Jagla pair potential (parameters in the Supplementary Text, not in the file), constant NVT with a Langevin thermostat; the unlike attraction E_AB is the energy scale, the like attractions E_AA and E_BB are given relative to it, and temperature as kT/E_AB. Free energies by an extension of the Einstein-molecule method to crystals with exposed surfaces, kT/E_AB from 0.02 to 0.11, 32-point Gauss-Legendre integration, sizes from 36, extrapolation to infinite size over sizes of 100 and more. The molecular dynamics at the same conditions puts the crossover nearer 144 particles; the authors attribute the difference to the time transformations take in larger crystallites and to layer sliding that thermodynamic integration suppresses.
